14: # README Template and Selection Guide
15: 
16: Use this template for project, skill, feature and component READMEs. Use [`readme-code-template.md`](./readme-code-template.md) for source-folder READMEs that explain package topology, files, boundaries and data or control flow.
17: 
18: ---
19: 
20: ## 1. README SELECTION
21: 
22: README files answer two questions: what is this, and how does someone use or navigate it?
23: 
24: | Type | Use When | Template |
25: |---|---|---|
26: | Project | The repository or package needs a public entry point | This file |
27: | Skill | A skill needs human-facing context beyond `SKILL.md` | This file |
28: | Feature | A user-facing feature needs setup, usage or behavior notes | This file |
29: | Component | A reusable module has an API, examples or configuration | This file, trimmed |
30: | Code Folder | A source directory needs developer orientation | [`readme-code-template.md`](./readme-code-template.md) |
31: 
32: Create a README when someone can land in the folder and need orientation. Skip it when inline comments or a nearby parent README already explain the folder.
33: 
34: ```text
35: Is this a project, package, skill or feature root?
36: +-- Yes: write a general README.
37: `-- No: is this source-code orientation?
38:     +-- Yes: use readme_code_template.md.
39:     `-- No: write a focused README only if readers need setup, usage or navigation help.
40: ```
41: 
42: Keep READMEs current-state only. Do not cite spec packet numbers, phase IDs or migration history. Use feature names, file paths, commands and stable source links.
43: 
44: ---
45: 
46: ## 2. GENERAL STRUCTURE
47: 
48: Use only the sections that fit the audience. Project and skill READMEs often need most sections. Feature and component READMEs should stay shorter.
49: 
50: | Section | Include When | Content |
51: |---|---|---|
52: | Overview | Always | Purpose, audience, main value and prerequisites |
53: | Key Statistics | Useful facts help readers decide scope | Counts, version, supported modes, limits |
54: | How This Compares | Readers may confuse this with nearby tools | Short comparison table |
55: | Quick Start | Readers need to run or try something | Short setup, verification and first use |
56: | Features | Capabilities need explanation | Feature groups, behavior notes and examples |
57: | Requirements | Runtime, tool or service needs exist | Minimum versions, permissions and external services |
58: | Structure | Navigation matters | Directory tree and key files |
59: | Configuration | Settings exist | Config files, options, defaults and env vars |
60: | Usage Examples | Patterns are easier shown than described | Simple and advanced examples with expected results |
61: | Troubleshooting | Users can hit known issues | What they see, cause and fix |
62: | FAQ | Repeated questions exist | Short answers only |
63: | Related Resources | Always when links exist | Grouped skills, documents, commands or external references |
64: 
65: Code-folder READMEs are different. Do not force Quick Start, Features, FAQ or Troubleshooting unless the directory has runnable commands or known reader problems. Use [`readme-code-template.md`](./readme-code-template.md).
66: 
67: ---
68: 
69: ## 3. SKILL AND PROJECT PROFILE
70: 
71: Use this profile for OpenCode skills, package roots and project-level READMEs that need more than a bare overview.
72: 
73: | Profile Block | Good For | Keep It Short By |
74: |---|---|---|
75: | `trigger_phrases` | Search, memory and skill routing | 3-8 concrete phrases |
76: | Key Statistics | Skill counts, tool counts, version facts | Use one compact table |
77: | How This Compares | Neighboring skills or tools | Compare only reader-relevant differences |
78: | Key Features | Current capability inventory | Group related features |
79: | Requirements | Tooling and runtime needs | Separate required from optional |
80: | Related Skills | Skill graph navigation | Group by relationship type |
81: | Related Documents | Operator or developer references | Link stable docs, not packet history |
82: | FAQ | Repeated questions | 3-6 high-value Q&A pairs |
83: 
84: Sections use plain numbered H2 headings. Do not add `<!-- ANCHOR -->` comments or a Table of Contents.
85: 
86: ```markdown
87: ## 1. OVERVIEW
88: 
89: [Section content]
90: 
91: ```
92: 
93: ---
94: 
95: ## 4. WRITING RULES
96: 
97: Write for scanning first.
98: 
99: - Lead with what the thing does.
100: - Put the fastest useful path before detailed reference.
101: - Use tables for options, file lists and comparisons.
102: - Give every inventory item a description. When an item needs more than one line, switch to the itemized pattern below instead of widening the table.
103: - Use fenced code blocks with language tags.
104: - Test commands before documenting them.
105: - Show expected output for verification commands.
106: - Use relative links for local docs.
107: - Remove unused sections instead of leaving placeholders.
108: 
109: The itemized pattern for inventories where each item needs more than one line:
110: 
111: ```markdown
112: **`spec.md`**
113: - What the feature is and why it exists.
114: - Required at every level.
115: ```
116: 
117: Group related items under an unnumbered `#####` heading when the inventory has natural groups, for example by how each item is triggered.
118: 
119: Voice by README type:
120: 
121: | Type | Voice |
122: |---|---|
123: | Project, Skill, Feature | Plain explanation first, reference detail later |
124: | Component | Technical and concise |
125: | Code Folder | Technical and concise, via `readme-code-template.md` |
126: 
127: Human Voice Rules apply to all README content:
128: 
129: - No em dashes. Use commas, periods or colons.
130: - No semicolons. Split the sentence or use "and".
131: - No Oxford comma in inline lists.
132: - No setup phrases.
133: - No banned words from the HVR reference.
134: - Prefer active voice and direct verbs.
135: 
136: Full reference: [`hvr-rules.md`](../../sk-create-with-human-voice/references/hvr-rules.md).
137: 
138: ---
139: 
140: ## 5. FRONTMATTER
141: 
142: Frontmatter is optional for normal project READMEs and recommended for skill or system documentation that should be discoverable.
143: 
144: ```yaml
145: ---
146: title: "[DOCUMENT_TITLE]"
147: description: "[One-sentence description]"
148: trigger_phrases:
149:   - "[search phrase]"
150:   - "[routing phrase]"
151: ---
152: ```
153: 
154: Use frontmatter when it improves routing, search or maintenance. Omit it for small human-only documents.
155: 
156: ---
157: 
158: ## 6. FILLABLE SCAFFOLD
159: 
160: Copy this scaffold, then remove sections that do not apply.
161: 
162: ````markdown
163: ---
164: title: "[PROJECT_OR_FEATURE_NAME]"
165: description: "[One-sentence description]"
166: trigger_phrases:
167:   - "[search phrase]"
168: version: 1.0.0.0
169: ---

186: | Version | [Version or release channel] |
187: | Main audience | [Who uses this] |
188: | Operating modes | [Mode count or short list] |
189: 
190: ### How This Compares
191: 
192: | Capability | This Project | Related Option |
193: |---|---|---|
194: | [Capability] | [Current behavior] | [Difference] |
195: 
196: 
197: ---
198:

200: 
201: ```bash
202: # Install or prepare
203: [command]
204:

206: [command]
207: ```

215: 
216: ### Key Features
217: 
218: | Feature | What It Does |
219: |---|---|
220: | [Feature] | [Current behavior] |

15: # Hermes Agent Delegation Reference
16: 
17: This reference prevents a category error: Hermes profiles and `delegate_task` sub-agents are not persona surfaces for this repo's agents.
18: 
19: ## 1. OVERVIEW
20: 
21: ### Core Principle
22: 
23: The repo's agents (`.skilled/agents/*.md`, the authored source) reach a Hermes dispatch only inside the prompt. Hermes has no flag that loads an agent file, its profiles are whole-home islands, and `delegate_task` children receive a goal and context, never an agent definition.
24: 
25: ---
26: 
27: ## 2. PERSONA ROUTES
28: 
29: | Route | Works | Use when |
30: |---|---|---|
31: | Inline the persona block at the top of the prompt, after the child-dispatch preamble | Yes | Default; the `cli-codex` and `cli-pi` precedent |
32: | Persona skill preloaded with `-s <name>` from `./.hermes/skills` | Yes, after the trust grant | Only if prompt size becomes a measured problem; needs the repo-local folder and the operator's trust |
33: | `hermes profile create` per agent | No | Profiles isolate homes and credentials, not personas |
34: | `hermes import-agent claude-code` | No | Imports `CLAUDE.md` into memories and copies skills into the user home; never imports agent files; bypasses trust and quarantine |
35: 
36: Resolve the persona from the calling runtime's agent directory (AGENTS.md §9), since Hermes has none of its own and its personas travel inlined in the prompt, and map each subtask to the right agent (code, review, design, deep-research, markdown). The canonical contract is `../../../sk-prompt/assets/cli-prompt-quality-card.md` "Persona Injection".
37: 
38: ---
39: 
40: ## 3. COMMANDS
41: 
42: The repo's nested commands under `.skilled/commands/**` have no Hermes equivalent: Hermes has no workflow engine and its slash commands are its own. The cli-pi precedent applies: flatten each command into a prompt template under `.hermes/prompts/` and carry it with `--query-file`. The runtime-folder phase generates those templates with a sync script; a dispatch loads the template text into its prompt file.
43: 
44: ---
45: 
46: ## 3A. PERSONA THROUGH THE REPO PLUGIN
47: 
48: `.hermes/agents/` links the shared runtime-neutral agent files, and `sync-skills-hermes.cjs` mirrors each as the preloadable skill `agent-<name>` because Hermes has no agent flag and caps a plugin prompt section at 4000 characters (a 22k persona in a section was skipped outright). The native-shaped dispatch is `-s agent-<name>` plus `HERMES_AGENT_PERSONA=<name>` with `HERMES_ENABLE_PROJECT_PLUGINS=1`: the skill carries the whole persona and the plugin's persona section binds it for the session. `--ignore-rules` is passed alongside `-s`: a live A/B under the flag showed the preload still reaching the model, so omitting it only bled SOUL.md, memories and session search into the leaf. Inline stays the fallback for a run without the plugin or the mirror.
49: 
50: ---
51: 
52: ## 4. SKILLS
53: 
54: With the repo trusted, Hermes loads the curated per-skill links under `.hermes/skills/<name>` and can preload one with `-s <name>` (observed 2026-09-14: `-s cli-hermes` quoted the packet's first hard rule). A dispatch that needs any other skill names it in the prompt by path, because only linked skills are visible to Hermes and the hub identity does not cross the link.
55: 
56: ---
57: 
58: ## 5. `delegate_task` AND THE DELEGATION BOUNDARY
59: 
60: Hermes's own sub-agents are spawned by the `delegation` toolset. A leaf lineage never carries that toolset: a sub-agent spawned inside a lineage runs outside the runner's containment and stack guards. For non-leaf use, the semantics of `delegation.subagent_auto_approve`, child timeouts and flag inheritance are open questions for the contract pin. Because Hermes has in-process delegation, `cli-hermes` is not exempt from the self-presence guards the way `cli-pi` is.
61: 
62: ---
63: 
64: ## 6. MCP AND HOOKS AS DELEGATION SURFACES
65: 
66: MCP servers are user-level ([mcp-policy.md](./mcp-policy.md)); the repo's guard cores reach a Hermes session through the project plugin ([hook-contract.md](./hook-contract.md)). 17: This reference prevents a category error: Hermes profiles and `delegate_task` sub-agents are not persona surfaces for this repo's agents.
18: 
19: ## 1. OVERVIEW
20: 
21: ### Purpose
22: 
23: Records every route a repo persona can take into a Hermes dispatch, and the reason a profile or a `delegate_task` child cannot stand in for one.
24: 
25: ### When to Use
26: 
27: - Composing a dispatch that carries a resolved agent persona
28: - Deciding whether to preload `agent-<name>` or inline the persona
29: - Checking what a `delegate_task` child may and may not do
30: - Finding the prompt template for a nested `.skilled/commands` command
31: 
32: ### Core Principle
33: 
34: The repo's agents (`.skilled/agents/*.md`, the authored source) reach a Hermes dispatch only inside the prompt. Hermes has no flag that loads an agent file, its profiles are whole-home islands, and `delegate_task` children receive a goal and context, never an agent definition.
35: 
36: ---
37: 
38: ## 2. PERSONA ROUTES
39: 
40: | Route | Works | Use when |
41: |---|---|---|
42: | Inline the persona block at the top of the prompt, after the child-dispatch preamble | Yes | Default; the `cli-codex` and `cli-pi` precedent |
43: | Persona skill preloaded with `-s <name>` from `./.hermes/skills` | Yes, after the trust grant | Only if prompt size becomes a measured problem; needs the repo-local folder and the operator's trust |
44: | `hermes profile create` per agent | No | Profiles isolate homes and credentials, not personas |
45: | `hermes import-agent claude-code` | No | Imports `CLAUDE.md` into memories and copies skills into the user home; never imports agent files; bypasses trust and quarantine |
46: 
47: Resolve the persona from the calling runtime's agent directory (AGENTS.md §9), since Hermes has none of its own and its personas travel inlined in the prompt, and map each subtask to the right agent (code, review, design, deep-research, markdown). The canonical contract is `../../../sk-prompt/assets/cli-prompt-quality-card.md` "Persona Injection".
48: 
49: ---
50: 
51: ## 3. COMMANDS
52: 
53: The repo's nested commands under `.skilled/commands/**` have no Hermes equivalent: Hermes has no workflow engine and its slash commands are its own. The cli-pi precedent applies: flatten each command into a prompt template under `.hermes/prompts/` and carry it with `--query-file`. The runtime-folder phase generates those templates with a sync script; a dispatch loads the template text into its prompt file.
54: 
55: ---
56: 
57: ## 4. PERSONA THROUGH THE REPO PLUGIN
58: 
59: `.hermes/agents/` links the shared runtime-neutral agent files, and `sync-skills-hermes.cjs` mirrors each as the preloadable skill `agent-<name>` because Hermes has no agent flag and caps a plugin prompt section at 4000 characters (a 22k persona in a section was skipped outright).
60: 
61: The native-shaped dispatch pairs:
62: 
63: - `-s agent-<name>`, the skill that carries the whole persona
64: - `HERMES_AGENT_PERSONA=<name>`, the name the plugin's persona section binds for the session
65: 
66: `HERMES_ENABLE_PROJECT_PLUGINS=1` must be set for the plugin to load.
67: 
68: `--ignore-rules` is passed alongside `-s`: a live A/B under the flag showed the preload still reaching the model, so omitting it only bled SOUL.md, memories and session search into the leaf. Inline stays the fallback for a run without the plugin or the mirror.
69: 
70: ---
71: 
72: ## 5. SKILLS
73: 
74: With the repo trusted, Hermes loads the curated per-skill links under `.hermes/skills/<name>` and can preload one with `-s <name>` (observed 2026-09-14: `-s cli-hermes` quoted the packet's first hard rule). A dispatch that needs any other skill names it in the prompt by path, because only linked skills are visible to Hermes and the hub identity does not cross the link.
75: 
76: ---
77: 
78: ## 6. `delegate_task` AND THE DELEGATION BOUNDARY
79: 
80: Hermes's own sub-agents are spawned by the `delegation` toolset. A leaf lineage never carries that toolset: a sub-agent spawned inside a lineage runs outside the runner's containment and stack guards. For non-leaf use, the semantics of `delegation.subagent_auto_approve`, child timeouts and flag inheritance are open questions for the contract pin. Because Hermes has in-process delegation, `cli-hermes` is not exempt from the self-presence guards the way `cli-pi` is.
81: 
82: ---
83: 
84: ## 7. MCP AND HOOKS AS DELEGATION SURFACES
85:

README.md:21:Hermes Agent is Nous Research's open-source Python agent CLI, installed as a git checkout under `~/.hermes` and reached through the `hermes` binary. README.md:23:The packet owns three things: the routing contract, the availability and provider probes, and prompt construction. It owns no spawn path. 15: # Hermes Agent Delegation Reference
16: 
17: This reference prevents a category error: Hermes profiles and `delegate_task` sub-agents are not persona surfaces for this repo's agents.
18: 
19: ## 1. OVERVIEW
20: 
21: ### Core Principle
22: 
23: The repo's agents (`.skilled/agents/*.md`, the authored source) reach a Hermes dispatch only inside the prompt. Hermes has no flag that loads an agent file, its profiles are whole-home islands, and `delegate_task` children receive a goal and context, never an agent definition.
24: 
25: ---
26: 
27: ## 2. PERSONA ROUTES
28: 
29: | Route | Works | Use when |
30: |---|---|---|
31: | Inline the persona block at the top of the prompt, after the child-dispatch preamble | Yes | Default; the `cli-codex` and `cli-pi` precedent |
32: | Persona skill preloaded with `-s <name>` from `./.hermes/skills` | Yes, after the trust grant | Only if prompt size becomes a measured problem; needs the repo-local folder and the operator's trust |
33: | `hermes profile create` per agent | No | Profiles isolate homes and credentials, not personas |
34: | `hermes import-agent claude-code` | No | Imports `CLAUDE.md` into memories and copies skills into the user home; never imports agent files; bypasses trust and quarantine |
35: 
36: Resolve the persona from the calling runtime's agent directory (AGENTS.md §9), since Hermes has none of its own and its personas travel inlined in the prompt, and map each subtask to the right agent (code, review, design, deep-research, markdown). The canonical contract is `../../../sk-prompt/assets/cli-prompt-quality-card.md` "Persona Injection".
37: 
38: ---
39: 
40: ## 3. COMMANDS
41: 
42: The repo's nested commands under `.skilled/commands/**` have no Hermes equivalent: Hermes has no workflow engine and its slash commands are its own. The cli-pi precedent applies: flatten each command into a prompt template under `.hermes/prompts/` and carry it with `--query-file`. The runtime-folder phase generates those templates with a sync script; a dispatch loads the template text into its prompt file.
43: 
44: ---
45: 
46: ## 3A. PERSONA THROUGH THE REPO PLUGIN
47: 
48: `.hermes/agents/` links the shared runtime-neutral agent files, and `sync-skills-hermes.cjs` mirrors each as the preloadable skill `agent-<name>` because Hermes has no agent flag and caps a plugin prompt section at 4000 characters (a 22k persona in a section was skipped outright). The native-shaped dispatch is `-s agent-<name>` plus `HERMES_AGENT_PERSONA=<name>` with `HERMES_ENABLE_PROJECT_PLUGINS=1`: the skill carries the whole persona and the plugin's persona section binds it for the session. `--ignore-rules` is passed alongside `-s`: a live A/B under the flag showed the preload still reaching the model, so omitting it only bled SOUL.md, memories and session search into the leaf. Inline stays the fallback for a run without the plugin or the mirror.
49: 
50: ---
51: 
52: ## 4. SKILLS
53: 
54: With the repo trusted, Hermes loads the curated per-skill links under `.hermes/skills/<name>` and can preload one with `-s <name>` (observed 2026-09-14: `-s cli-hermes` quoted the packet's first hard rule). A dispatch that needs any other skill names it in the prompt by path, because only linked skills are visible to Hermes and the hub identity does not cross the link.
55: 
56: ---
57: 
58: ## 5. `delegate_task` AND THE DELEGATION BOUNDARY
59: 
60: Hermes's own sub-agents are spawned by the `delegation` toolset. A leaf lineage never carries that toolset: a sub-agent spawned inside a lineage runs outside the runner's containment and stack guards. For non-leaf use, the semantics of `delegation.subagent_auto_approve`, child timeouts and flag inheritance are open questions for the contract pin. Because Hermes has in-process delegation, `cli-hermes` is not exempt from the self-presence guards the way `cli-pi` is.
61: 
62: ---
63: 
64: ## 6. MCP AND HOOKS AS DELEGATION SURFACES
65: 
66: MCP servers are user-level ([mcp-policy.md](./mcp-policy.md)); the repo's guard cores reach a Hermes session through the project plugin ([hook-contract.md](./hook-contract.md)). 15: # Hermes Agent Delegation Reference

19: ## 1. OVERVIEW
20: 
21: ### Purpose
22: 
23: Records every route a repo persona can take into a Hermes dispatch, and the reason a profile or a `delegate_task` child cannot stand in for one.
24: 
25: ### When to Use
26: 
27: - Composing a dispatch that carries a resolved agent persona
28: - Deciding whether to preload `agent-<name>` or inline the persona
29: - Checking what a `delegate_task` child may and may not do
30: - Finding the prompt template for a nested `.skilled/commands` command
31: 
32: ### Core Principle
33: 
34: The repo's agents (`.skilled/agents/*.md`, the authored source) reach a Hermes dispatch only inside the prompt. Hermes has no flag that loads an agent file, its profiles are whole-home islands, and `delegate_task` children receive a goal and context, never an agent definition.
